_comment: The controlled vocabulary. The renderer takes its display labels from here and the validator checks data/systems.json against it, so adding a term means editing this file first. Definitions are deliberately opinionated — see CONTRIBUTING.md before proposing a new one.

graph.label: graph
graph.definition: Modules with ports; connections are drawn by the user. The topology is the patch.

rack.label: rack
rack.definition: Ordered slots that signal falls through. Modulation is a separate mechanism, not another cable.

matrix.label: matrix
matrix.definition: The same routing without cables: sources against destinations in a grid. Compact, unreadable at a glance.

code.label: code
code.definition: Assembly by text. Included only where the work is mostly wiring premade modules rather than writing DSP from scratch.

format.label: format
format.definition: Not a system. A contract that lets modules exist and travel. Filed separately so it is never compared like for like against an environment.

midi.label: midi
midi.definition: Processes notes or MIDI as a patchable domain, not only as I/O.

export.label: export
export.definition: Emits an artifact that runs somewhere else — a plugin, firmware, source code.

encap.label: encap
encap.definition: Users can build a reusable module with its own interface, not merely copy a group of modules.

open.label: open
open.definition: Open-source licence on the system itself. Module ecosystems may differ.

verified.definition: Checked against a vendor page, official documentation, or another primary source. Requires a source URL.

reported.definition: Reported by press, a maintainer's blog, or a forum thread. Requires a source URL.

unverified.definition: Asserted from memory or general knowledge, not checked. Must NOT carry a source URL — if you have one, the claim is verified or reported.

midi.label: midi
midi.definition: Takes notes in, sends notes out, or both. See the claims for which.

inspection.label: Seeing the signal
inspection.definition: Ways the system shows you what is actually happening in the patch.

hotswap.label: Changing things while they run
hotswap.definition: Whether the patch can be rewired without stopping, and what that costs.

mapping.label: Binding controls
mapping.definition: How a control gets attached to a parameter.

reuse.label: Making a thing reusable
reuse.definition: How work is packaged so it can be used again or by someone else.

variation.label: Variation and chance
variation.definition: Randomisation, morphing, locking, and other ways of moving through a patch space.

timing.label: Timing resolution
timing.definition: The granularity at which events and modulation actually land.

access.label: Where you sit while patching
access.definition: The physical and interface circumstances of use — screen, browser, touch, none.

tuning.label: Pitch and tuning
tuning.definition: How pitch is organised, including microtonal and non-12-EDO support.
